study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Ge et al., The Lancet Digital Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of brain morphometry across the lifespan with CentileBrain: algorithm benchmarking and model optimisation

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Benchmark and identify the optimal normative modeling approach for brain morphometric data by comparing algorithms and covariate choices, and quantify performance and stability across age and sample sizes.

rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: "We collated de-identified data from 87 datasets from Europe, Australia, the USA, South Africa, and east Asia ... Data use aligned with the policies of the ENIGMA Lifespan Working Group"

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Diagnostic classification via linear SVC using regional Z-scores vs observed measures with 5-fold CV (100 repeats) and permutation tests; symptom severity prediction via ridge regression on principal components with 5-fold CV (100 repeats) and permutation testing.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: MFPR with non-linear age and global covariates outperformed alternatives; performance plateaued at ~3000 samples; Z-scores improved psychosis classification over observed measures and showed longitudinal stability.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Using 37,407 healthy individuals from 87 datasets, MFPR emerged as optimal, with non-linear age and linear global measures as covariates. Performance (MAE/RMSE) plateaued at N≈3000 and was robust across age bins (r>0.98). Z-scores from optimised MFPR improved HCP-EP diagnostic SVC accuracy (AUC 0.63, p<0.001) versus observed data (AUC 0.49), and normative Z-scores were stable over ~2-year intervals in SLIM and QTAB longitudinal cohorts.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Under-representation of some age ranges; limited longitudinal duration; generalisability to specific ancestries untested; not all potential covariates included (e.g., adversity, prematurity, SES); adding many covariates may reduce applicability across datasets.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: "There are several methodological limitations ... could benefit from the inclusion of more young and middle-aged adults and data from longitudinal follow-up over long periods ... Testing the generalisability of our models to populations with specific ancestries is an important next step. We did not include an exhaustive list of potential explanatory variables ... such as childhood adversity, premature birth, or socioeconomic status ... the inclusion of multiple explanatory variables ... could restrict its applicability ..."

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Models and scripts available via CentileBrain; sex-specific ROI-wise models (150 measures); guidance that performance saturates at ~3000 participants can inform study planning.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Training/test split stratified by site and age; outlier removal at >1.5×IQR per subset; FreeSurfer 7.1.0 used for HCP-EP processing; ENIGMA/ABCD/Qoala-T QC mix; compared site random effects vs ComBat-GAM (similar MFPR performance).
